answer_to_strategic_question.question: Did Framework v2 deliver measurable operational gains during a real certification wave?
answer_to_strategic_question.detail: Framework v2 delivered measurable, meaningful gains across 5 of 6 dimensions in its first real certification wave (S852–S854). The 6th dimension (delta review) is inherently not exercisable in a first wave — it requires a comparative baseline from a prior certification. The gains are real, measured, and verified against live pack state.

evidence.pre_flight: 351 false positives intercepted — the exact DL-029 scenario v2 was architected to prevent
evidence.governance: 10 automated checks replacing hours of manual verification
evidence.generation: 0 human decision points in orchestrator pipeline
evidence.delta_review: Architecture proven, data deferred to S811+

answer_to_strategic_question.caveat: The P3 target (3.8×) depends on delta review and board consolidation — both valid architectural projections but not yet exercisable. The gap from 2.43× to 3.8× is closeable with: (a) a second certification wave enabling delta comparison (~2.0×), and (b) adoption of the v2 5-board model (~1.3×). These are not infrastructure gaps — they are sequencing gaps.
answer_to_strategic_question.confidence: HIGH (5/6 dimensions have real measured data). MEDIUM (P3 target depends on unexercised components — valid projection, not measured).

s353_verdict: FRAMEWORK_V2_FIRST_CERTIFICATION_SUCCESS — The first Framework v2 certification wave (S852–S854) delivered measurable throughput gains (2.43× effective, exceeding P1 target), prevented 351 false positives from contaminating certification decisions (anti-DL-029 architecture proven), eliminated manual governance overhead (10 automated checks), achieved 100% queue conversion with zero regressions, and demonstrated the orchestrator pipeline can operate autonomously. The single unrealized gain (delta review) is a sequencing constraint, not an infrastructure gap. Framework v2 is delivering on its architectural promises.
